alignments.note: Supplied subject pronoun rides with the verb; discontinuous under rule 15.
Passive auxiliary is the verb's own helper.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun only; the ASV writes two words, so the ordinary split applies (rules 32, 90).
Relativizer is the participle's helper; 'over' realizes the peri- preverb inside the verb's unit (rule 106).
Genitive article carries the case preposition and is headed on 'the' (rule 21).

klasma is a result nominal whose English noun 'pieces' is a real gloss, as ktisma to 'created thing' is, so rule 66's first arm heads on the noun and not on 'broken'. Corrected at reconciliation from a head on 'broken': the corpus spends 'pieces' on this lexeme in all eight of its units across five chapters, MAT.14.20 in this book among them, and 'broken' in none, so rules 84 and 91 leave the head not in doubt and the earlier hedge is withdrawn.
Supplied subject rides with the verb; 'up' is the English particle of the phrasal rendering, airo being uncompounded so no source token stands to answer to it.

review_notes: s010's head was the one materially contested choice in this verse and is now settled on 'pieces' by unanimous corpus precedent, MAT.14.20 included; the competing head on 'broken' does not stand.
s011's 'up' stays inside the verb's unit as the English phrasal particle, airo carrying no preverb, which is how MAT.14.20 reads the identical clause.
